decision: Keep quality as default. Clarity is opt-in: full-input coverage improved on one video, but existing selected views did not become sharper and real-time stability/identity accuracy are not established.

unchanged: good_enough and lock windows use composite quality
policy.warning: Candidate ordering changes which precise/verification calls are attempted and can interact with failure backoff; total call counts need measurement.

method.hardware: Intel Core i9-13980HX, Windows CPUExecutionProvider; RTX 4060 unused.
method.realtime: Original PTS; capacity-1 latest queue; serial quality A / clarity A / clarity B / quality B; reverse video order in B; no profiler.
method.pooling: Individual frame timings pooled, never an average of percentiles.
limitations: All eight real-time videos dropped frames; none is an equal-work comparison.
Both strategies were substantially slower than the 2026-11-15 session. CPU frequency and external load were not locked; the slowdown is not attributed to this policy.
Real-time drops changed selected frames; clarity did not consistently retain the new right-view capture.
Two videos have no identity-match labels; no ReID accuracy or broad clarity superiority claim.
No new phone throughput/energy or real-model browser benchmark.

chain: Both policies accepted frame 144 into the unconfirmed right-view buffer.
At 145 quality ranked the coarse .866872 above pending .852313, ran precise localization, failed view_unconfirmed, then set a .25 s retry delay.
Clarity ranked the coarse .817204 below pending .850914 and skipped that attempted replacement, so no failed-candidate retry delay was created.
After the unconfirmed visit ended, frame 148 passed all original gates under clarity and was confirmed at 151; quality was still in retry backoff at 148.
right_capture_explanation.interpretation: A scheduling/backoff consequence of ranking, not evidence of looser thresholds or uniformly sharper photos.
